To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The substrate choice has a strong effect on the measured Seebeck coefficient, and (2) The measured Seebeck coefficient is strongly affected by the layer thickness and the spatial distribution of the material properties.

(1) thermally poor conducting substrata are preferred for thermopower measurements of thin film composition libraries, (2) the substrate material has an influence on the measured thermopowers of the thin films, (3) the spatial resolution of the thermopower measurements is strongly affected by the substrate material, and (4) thermally poor conductive substrates suffer from a lower accuracy of the measured thermovoltage, which is caused by local temperature gradients in the film.

the thermopower of thin film composition libraries on lowly conductible substrates is underestimated due to the thermal coupling to the substrate and due to the inhomogeneous distribution of thermopower in the films.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the interrelation between the thermopower measurement conditions, material properties, and the substrate material, which has to be considered for a meaningful evaluation of combinatorial material libraries.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thermopower measurement of thin films is strongly affected by the thermal conductivity of the substrate material as well as the film thickness.

the substrate material and the spatial distribution of properties within a material library should be considered carefully for high-throughput characterization of thermopowers of thin film combinatorial libraries.
the accuracy of the thermopower measurement is strongly affected by the substrate material, and the spatial resolution is strongly affected by thermal conductivity of the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PSM can be used for the identification of promising materials within a composition spread library.
the PSM is capable of measuring thermopower with an accuracy of about ±10% and that the accuracy is not significantly influenced by substrate material or film thickness.
the PSM method is a powerful tool for the identification of TE material properties in combinatorial material libraries, but the choice of the substrate material is of crucial importance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the accuracy of the thermopower measurements is strongly affected by the thermal and electrical properties of the substrates and the film thickness, and that local thermopower measurements are prone to additional errors due to spatially varying properties.
the substrate material and the spatial distribution of the material properties have a strong influence on the accuracy of the measured thermoelectric properties.
the substrate material and its thermal conductivity have to be considered for accurate and reliable measurements of thermopower in thin film composition spread material libraries.
